topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Concept
lecture_lines: Average speed equals total distance divided by time.
Visualize this as a line connecting two points.
The line slope represents the average speed.
animations: Display title: The Average Speed Concept. Color #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Problem of 'Instantaneous' Speed
lecture_lines: Can we find speed at one exact moment?
A single point makes our formula fail.
We must shrink the interval to approach zero.
animations: Display title: The Problem of Instantaneous Speed. Color #FFFFFF.
Show a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/particle.svg] moving along a non-linear path. Color #FFFFFF.
Highlight the challenge: how to define speed at one point? Color #FF0000.

sections.title: The Limit Process: Approaching the Tangent
lecture_lines: As time shrinks, the secant line tilts.
It eventually becomes a tangent line.
This tangent slope shows instantaneous speed.
Point Q slides closer to point P.
The limit defines the exact rate change.
animations: Display title: The Limit Process. Color #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg]
Show a sequence of secant lines getting closer to a tangent. Color #FFFF00.
Highlight the tangent line at point P. Color #00FF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg]

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
lecture_lines: The derivative defines the limit process.
It measures instantaneous change precisely.
Apply the difference quotient limit formula.
This finds slope at any point x.
A powerful tool for complex curves.
animations: Display title: Defining the Derivative. Color #FFFFFF.
Present the limit definition formula clearly. Color #FFFFFF.
Use arrows [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg] to connect terms in formula to the geometric visualization. Colors: Delta y #FF0000, Delta x #00FF00.

sections.title: Application: Real-world Significance
lecture_lines: Derivatives reveal local function behavior.
Used for velocity, growth, and cost.
Essential for understanding real-world systems.
Calculate exact speeds for moving objects.
Apply math to dynamic, changing phenomena.
